## Overview

OpenCode's marketing site is rendered entirely in Berkeley Mono — every word on the page, from the 38px hero headline down to the 14px footer fine print, sits in the same monospaced face. The visual identity comes from that single typographic decision: the page reads like a manpage or a static-site README, complete with bracketed `[+]` / `[-]` / `[x]` ASCII markers used in place of icons or bullets, and a wordmark rendered as block-pixel ASCII art at the top of the nav. There is no sans-serif anywhere, no display face, no italics, no decorative ornament — the system is one font and one weight away from being a 1990s `whatis` page rendered at modern resolutions.

The chrome is austere: warm cream canvas (`{colors.canvas}` — `#fdfcfc` with a faint blush), nearly-black ink (`{colors.ink}` — `#201d1d`), and a 4-tier neutral gray ladder for body, metadata, and disabled text. Cards don't exist as raised surfaces — sections are just hairline-bordered text blocks (`{colors.hairline}` 1px) sitting directly on the canvas with `{spacing.section}` (96px) air between them. The single "visual" moment in the entire system is a full-bleed dark hero card (`{colors.surface-dark}` — true near-black) that mocks up the OpenCode TUI itself: a terminal frame with `tab` / `ctrl-p` keybinding hints, a "Build" command line, and the OpenCode wordmark rendered as a pixel-block ASCII title.

The semantic palette is unusual for a brand-marketing site: it ships the full Apple Human Interface Guidelines accent ramp — `{colors.accent}` (Apple Blue `#007aff`), `{colors.danger}` (`#ff3b30`), `{colors.warning}` (`#ff9f0a`), `{colors.success}` (`#30d158`) plus their hover/active deepenings — even though the marketing surfaces themselves only use these colors in the dark hero TUI mockup as syntax-highlight stand-ins. The wider palette belongs to the in-product TUI; the marketing pages mostly stay in monochrome.

**Key Characteristics:**
- 100% Berkeley Mono typography across every text role — no sans-serif fallback anywhere in the chrome
- Warm cream `{colors.canvas}` (#fdfcfc) as the only body background — no surface alternation across sections
- Single dark surface (`{colors.surface-dark}` — #201d1d) reserved exclusively for the hero TUI mockup
- 4px radius (`{rounded.sm}`) on every interactive element; sections themselves are sharp rectangles bordered in 1px hairline
- ASCII bracket markers (`[+]`, `[-]`, `[x]`) used as bullet glyphs in feature lists and FAQ rows
- Block-pixel ASCII wordmark in the primary nav and inside the hero TUI — the brand identity is its own ASCII art
- 96px `{spacing.section}` rhythm between every section, with no decorative dividers; only thin 1px `{colors.hairline}` rules separate content blocks

## Colors

> **Source pages:** `/` (home), `/zen`, `/enterprise`. The chrome palette is identical across all three.

### Brand & Accent
- **Ink** (`{colors.primary}` / `{colors.ink}` — `#201d1d`): the brand's only "color." Headlines, body text, primary CTA fill, nav links, and every solid icon. Treats nearly-black as the brand color rather than pure black to keep type readable on the warm cream canvas.
- **Ink Deep** (`{colors.ink-deep}` — `#0f0000`): pressed-state for the primary CTA. Carries a faint red undertone matching the canvas's warm cast.
- **Cream** (`{colors.canvas}` — `#fdfcfc`): the brand's signature warm white. Used for every page body, every card surface, the on-primary text color, and the ASCII wordmark fill on dark.

### Surface
- **Canvas Cream** (`{colors.canvas}` — `#fdfcfc`): every page body, every card.
- **Soft Surface** (`{colors.surface-soft}` — `#f8f7f7`): text-input default background, testimonial row fill, alternating row tint.
- **Surface Card** (`{colors.surface-card}` — `#f1eeee`): install-snippet pill, disabled button fill, slightly-elevated section row.
- **Surface Dark** (`{colors.surface-dark}` — `#201d1d`): the hero TUI mockup background and the dark CTA pill on the home page. Identical to `{colors.ink}` — the brand uses one near-black for both text and dark surfaces.
- **Surface Dark Elevated** (`{colors.surface-dark-elevated}` — `#302c2c`): the prompt-row inside the hero TUI mockup, one notch lighter than the dark surface itself.
- **Hairline** (`{colors.hairline}` — `rgba(15,0,0,0.12)`): 1px section divider. The translucent warm tint matches the cream canvas's undertone.
- **Hairline Strong** (`{colors.hairline-strong}` — `#646262`): tab strip's bottom rule and stronger inline divider.

### Text
- **Ink** (`{colors.ink}` — `#201d1d`): headlines, body text, primary nav links, button text on light surfaces.
- **Charcoal** (`{colors.charcoal}` — `#302c2c`): subtly softer body where pure ink is too heavy.
- **Body** (`{colors.body}` — `#424245`): default paragraph text and FAQ answers.
- **Mute** (`{colors.mute}` — `#646262`): tab labels (default state), metadata, footer link text, in-list secondary annotations.
- **Stone** (`{colors.stone}` — `#6e6e73`): least-emphasis utility text, breadcrumb separators.
- **Ash** (`{colors.ash}` — `#9a9898`): disabled text and secondary annotation in dark TUI mockup, also TUI mockup secondary color.

### Semantic
The full Apple Human Interface Guidelines semantic ramp ships with the system. On marketing pages these colors appear primarily inside the hero TUI mockup as syntax-highlight stand-ins; in the in-product TUI they carry their conventional meaning.

- **Accent** (`{colors.accent}` — `#007aff`): primary informational signal, in-product link color, TUI command highlight.
- **Accent Hover** (`{colors.accent-hover}` — `#0056b3`): pressed informational link.
- **Accent Active** (`{colors.accent-active}` — `#004085`): deeply-pressed informational state.
- **Danger** (`{colors.danger}` — `#ff3b30`): destructive confirmation, error state.
- **Danger Hover** (`{colors.danger-hover}` — `#d70015`): pressed destructive.
- **Danger Active** (`{colors.danger-active}` — `#a50011`): deeply-pressed destructive.
- **Warning** (`{colors.warning}` — `#ff9f0a`): caution callouts.
- **Warning Hover** (`{colors.warning-hover}` — `#cc7f08`): pressed caution.
- **Warning Active** (`{colors.warning-active}` — `#995f06`): deeply-pressed caution.
- **Success** (`{colors.success}` — `#30d158`): positive confirmation, in-TUI success indicator.

## Typography

### Font Family
**Berkeley Mono** is the proprietary monospaced face used across every text role in the system. It carries weights 400 (regular), 500 (medium), and 700 (bold) and falls back through a long monospace stack — IBM Plex Mono → ui-monospace → SFMono-Regular → Menlo → Monaco → Consolas → Liberation Mono → Courier New.

The single-font decision is the brand. There is no display face, no body sans, no italic alternative, and no fallback to a proportional font anywhere — even the legal copyright row uses Berkeley Mono at 14px. This is the most aggressive typographic restraint of any site in the marketing-tools category: OpenCode's identity is "the marketing page is a man page."

### Hierarchy

| Token | Size | Weight | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{typography.display-xl}` | 38px | 700 | 1.5 | 0 | Hero headline ("The open source AI coding agent") |
| `{typography.heading-md}` | 16px | 700 | 1.5 | 0 | Section label ("What is OpenCode?", "FAQ", "Built for privacy first") |
| `{typography.body-md}` | 16px | 400 | 1.5 | 0 | Body copy, paragraph text, list-row text, install-snippet code |
| `{typography.body-strong}` | 16px | 500 | 1.5 | 0 | Inline emphasis, primary nav link, tab-label active |
| `{typography.body-tight}` | 16px | 500 | 1 | 0 | Compact label rendered without breathing room |
| `{typography.link-md}` | 16px | 400 | 1.5 | 0 | Inline anchor link in body prose |
| `{typography.button-md}` | 16px | 500 | 2 | 0 | Every button label across the system |
| `{typography.caption-md}` | 14px | 400 | 2 | 0 | Footer link text, badge label, copyright row, chart caption |

### Principles
The hierarchy is built almost entirely from size and weight contrast on a single face. The display headline (38px / 700) and the heading-md label (16px / 700) share a weight; the difference is just size. Body and link share size, weight, and line-height — only context distinguishes them. Buttons get a deliberately tall line-height (2.0) so labels feel calmly spaced inside the 4px-radius rectangle.

### Note on Font Substitutes
Berkeley Mono is a paid commercial font. Open-source substitutes that approximate its metrics within ~3% at body sizes:
- **JetBrains Mono** — closest match for stroke contrast and x-height; pair at weights 400 / 500 / 700.
- **IBM Plex Mono** — official secondary fallback in the documented font stack; slightly more open counters but matches line-height behavior.
- **Geist Mono** — modern alternative with similar geometric construction.

When substituting, line-height behavior is preserved by keeping `lineHeight: 1.5` for body and `lineHeight: 2` for buttons — adjusting weight is rarely needed.

## Layout

### Spacing System
- **Base unit:** 8px (with finer 1/2/4px steps available for tight inline gaps).
- **Tokens (front matter):** `{spacing.xxs}` (1px) · `{spacing.xs}` (4px) · `{spacing.sm}` (8px) · `{spacing.md}` (12px) · `{spacing.lg}` (16px) · `{spacing.xl}` (24px) · `{spacing.xxl}` (32px) · `{spacing.section}` (96px).
- **Universal section rhythm:** every page in the set uses `{spacing.section}` (96px) as the vertical gap between major content blocks. This is the largest spacing token in the system and is the dominant layout cue across the home, `/zen`, and `/enterprise` pages.
- **Section internal padding:** content rows inside a section sit at `{spacing.lg}` (16px) vertical with no horizontal padding — text starts flush at the section's left edge.

### Grid & Container
- **Max width:** ~960px content column for body sections; the dark hero TUI mockup is full-bleed within an outer ~1100px content frame.
- **Two-column split:** `/enterprise` pairs a left text block (~360px wide) with a right-aligned form column (~480px wide). The home page is single-column reading.
- **Footer:** 5-up horizontal link row (GitHub / Docs / Changelog / Discord / X) at desktop, collapsing to 2-up at tablet and 1-up at mobile.

### Whitespace Philosophy
Whitespace is structural and generous. Sections sit 96px apart with no decorative dividers between them — the `{colors.hairline}` 1px rule is the only signal of separation. Inside a section, content is left-flush against the column edge with no internal indentation; bullets use ASCII bracket prefixes (`[+]` / `[-]`) instead of indent-based layout. The result is a page that feels like a printed code listing rather than a styled marketing layout.

## Elevation & Depth

| Level | Treatment | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 0 — Flat | No border, no shadow | Default for body sections, list rows, hero text block, footer |
| 1 — Hairline rule | 1px solid `{colors.hairline}` (translucent warm tint) | Section dividers, between major content blocks |
| 2 — Hairline strong | 1px solid `{colors.hairline-strong}` | Tab strip bottom rule, in-list emphasized divider |
| 3 — Inverted dark | `{colors.surface-dark}` fill | Hero TUI mockup, dark CTA pill — the system's only "elevated" surface uses color, not shadow |

There are no drop shadows in the system. Nothing lifts, nothing floats. The only way an element registers as "above" another is the dark surface used in the hero mockup.

### Decorative Depth
Depth comes from typography density and the single dark TUI mockup, not from CSS effects:
- **ASCII block-pixel wordmark** — the OpenCode brand name rendered as a 5-row block of monospaced character cells, used in the primary nav and as the centerpiece of the hero TUI mockup.
- **Hero TUI mockup** — full-bleed `{colors.surface-dark}` rectangle containing a faux terminal interface: ASCII wordmark, a `tui-prompt-row` showing a Build command line, and `tab switch agent` / `ctrl-p commands` keybinding hints in `{colors.ash}` at the bottom edge.
- **Chart tiles** — three thin-line ASCII charts inside the home page's "open source AI coding agent" stat block, with abstract dotted/sparse-line plots in `{colors.body}` against the cream canvas. Captions sit beneath in `{typography.caption-md}` (`Fig 1. 150K GitHub Stars`, `Fig 2. 850 Contributors`, `Fig 3. 6.5M Monthly Devs`).

## Shapes

### Border Radius Scale

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{rounded.none}` | 0px | Sections, hero TUI mockup, primary nav, footer, list rows — every container that isn't a button |
| `{rounded.sm}` | 4px | Every interactive element — primary CTA, secondary CTA, text inputs, install snippet, badges, prompt rows |
| `{rounded.full}` | 9999px | Avatar circles in testimonials |

The radius vocabulary is two values: 4px for interactive elements and 0px for everything else. Avatar circles in testimonial rows are the only fully-rounded element in the system.

### Photography Geometry
There is no photography. Visual elements are limited to:
- **ASCII block-pixel wordmark** in the nav and hero TUI mockup.
- **Inline ASCII charts** inside the stat-block section — abstract sparse-line and dotted plots without specific data points.
- **Avatar dots** (~32px) inside testimonial rows on `/zen` — flat colored circles in `{rounded.full}`.
- **In-product icons** (kbd, A+, ⊕, ↻, K, Z) rendered as small monospaced character glyphs, not bitmaps or SVG.

## Components

> **No hover states documented** per system policy. Each spec covers Default and Active/Pressed only.

### Buttons

**`button-primary`** — the universal OpenCode CTA
- Background `{colors.primary}`, text `{colors.on-primary}`, type `{typography.button-md}`, padding `4px 20px`, height ~36px, rounded `{rounded.sm}` (4px).
- Used for "Download" (top nav), "Get started with Zen", "Send" (enterprise contact form), "Subscribe" (newsletter footer), "Read docs →".
- Pressed state lives in `button-primary-active` — background drops to `{colors.ink-deep}`.

**`button-secondary`** — outlined alternative
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, 1px solid `{colors.hairline-strong}` border, type `{typography.button-md}`, padding `4px 20px`, rounded `{rounded.sm}`.
- Lower-emphasis CTA — appears beside the primary fill where two actions are paired.

**`button-tab`** + **`button-tab-active`** — install-tab strip
- Default: transparent background, text `{colors.mute}`, type `{typography.button-md}`, padding `8px 16px`, rounded `{rounded.none}`.
- Active: same surface, text `{colors.ink}`, with a 2px `{colors.ash}` bottom underline indicating selection.
- Used in the install-method tab strip on the home page (`curl` / `npm` / `bun` / `brew` / `yay`).

**`button-disabled`**
- Background `{colors.surface-card}`, text `{colors.ash}`, rounded `{rounded.sm}`.

### Badges & Chips

**`badge-news`** — small dark chip in the news/announcement strip
- Background `{colors.surface-dark}`, text `{colors.on-dark}`, type `{typography.caption-md}`, padding `2px 8px`, rounded `{rounded.sm}`.
- Sits inline with body copy as a "News" / "Beta" / "Live now" tag on the home page above the hero headline.

**`badge-section-label`** — bracketed section header
- Background transparent, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.heading-md}`, rounded `{rounded.none}`.
- Renders as a bare `**Heading**` line above a 1px `{colors.hairline}` rule with no chip background — but the way the text reads ("[+]", "[x]", `What is OpenCode?`) makes it function as a label component.

### Inputs & Forms

**`text-input`** + **`text-input-focused`**
- Default: background `{colors.surface-soft}`, text `{colors.ink}`, 1px solid `{colors.hairline}`, type `{typography.body-md}`, padding `8px 12px`, height ~40px, rounded `{rounded.sm}`.
- Focused: background flips to `{colors.canvas}`, border becomes 1px solid `{colors.ink}` (the canvas's flat focus signal — no halo, no glow).
- Used for every contact-form field on `/enterprise` (Full name, Role, Company, Company email, Phone number) and the newsletter email field at the home page footer.

**`textarea`**
- Background `{colors.surface-soft}`, text `{colors.ink}`, 1px solid `{colors.hairline}`, type `{typography.body-md}`, padding `12px`, rounded `{rounded.sm}`.
- "What problem are you trying to solve?" multi-line textarea on `/enterprise`.

**`install-snippet`** — the home page's signature install code block
- Background `{colors.surface-card}` (`#f1eeee`), text `{colors.ink}` rendered in `{typography.body-md}` (already monospaced — Berkeley Mono), padding `12px 16px`, rounded `{rounded.sm}`.
- Contains the literal `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash` command with a small copy-icon at the right edge. Sits below the install-method tab strip.

### Cards & Containers

**`hero-tui-mockup`** — the home page's signature TUI preview
- Container: full-bleed `{colors.surface-dark}` (~near-black), padding `64px 32px`, rounded `{rounded.none}`.
- Contents (top → bottom): ASCII block-pixel "OPENCODE" wordmark centered in `{colors.on-dark}`; a `{component.tui-prompt-row}` showing a "Build" command line with model selector text; an `tab switch agent  ctrl-p commands` keybinding hint row at the bottom in `{colors.ash}`.

**`tui-prompt-row`** — the inset command line inside the TUI mockup
- Background `{colors.surface-dark-elevated}` (`#302c2c`), text `{colors.on-dark}` in `{typography.body-md}`, padding `8px 12px`, rounded `{rounded.sm}`.
- Renders an inline command (`Build  Claude Opus 4.5  OpenCode Zen`) with a leading vertical pipe and the model name styled as a bracketed token.

**`list-row`** — feature/benefit row with ASCII bracket bullet
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.body}` in `{typography.body-md}`, padding `8px 0`.
- Each row begins with a `[+]` / `[-]` / `[x]` ASCII marker followed by a bold label and a regular description: e.g., `[+] LSP enabled    Automatically loads the right LSPs for the IDE`. The bracket marker is part of the text content, not a separate icon.

**`faq-row`** — FAQ entry with bracket toggle
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}` in `{typography.body-md}`, padding `12px 0`, with a 1px `{colors.hairline}` bottom rule.
- Each row leads with `+` / `−` ASCII markers indicating expand/collapse state. Always rendered as plain text rows — no chevron icons, no animated accordion chrome.

**`testimonial-row`** — `/zen` peer-quote row
- Background `{colors.surface-soft}`, text `{colors.body}` in `{typography.body-md}`, padding `16px 20px`, rounded `{rounded.sm}`.
- Layout: a 32px avatar circle (`{rounded.full}`) at left, name + role + company in `{typography.body-strong}` on the first line, quote in `{typography.body-md}` `{colors.body}` on the second line.

**`chart-tile`** — the stat-block sparse-line chart
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.body}` in `{typography.caption-md}`, rounded `{rounded.none}`, padding `16px`.
- Contains an inline SVG/CSS-drawn ASCII-style sparse-line plot (dotted, abstract — never specific data points) with a `Fig N. <stat label>` caption beneath in `{colors.mute}`.

### Navigation

**`primary-nav`**
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}` in `{typography.body-strong}`, height ~56px, rounded `{rounded.none}`, with a 1px `{colors.hairline}` bottom rule.
- Layout (desktop): block-pixel ASCII OpenCode wordmark at left (~120×24px), nav links cluster center-right ("GitHub [150K] · Docs · Zen · Go · Enterprise"), `{component.button-primary}` "Download" CTA at the far right with a small download glyph.

**Top Nav (Mobile)**
- ASCII wordmark stays at left, nav links collapse into a hamburger drawer at the right. The Download CTA remains visible at every breakpoint.

### Footer

**`footer-section`**
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.body}` in `{typography.caption-md}`, padding `32px 0`, with a 1px `{colors.hairline}` top rule.
- Top row: 5-column horizontal link grid (GitHub [150K] · Docs · Changelog · Discord · X), each rendered as a centered cell separated by 1px `{colors.hairline}` vertical rules.
- Bottom row: `©2026 Anomaly` copyright at left, `Brand · Privacy · Terms · English ▼` utility cluster at right, all in `{typography.caption-md}` `{colors.mute}`.

### Inline

**`link-inline`** — body-prose anchor link
- `{colors.ink}` text with underline. The brand's only link affordance — even links inside body paragraphs use ink color rather than `{colors.accent}` blue. Apple Blue is reserved for the in-product TUI.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Render every text role in Berkeley Mono. The single-font decision is the entire identity.
- Keep `{colors.canvas}` (`#fdfcfc`) as the only body background. Don't introduce gray section bands.
- Use ASCII bracket markers (`[+]`, `[-]`, `[x]`, `+`, `−`) as bullets, toggles, and section glyphs. They are the brand's only iconography.
- Anchor the dark `{component.hero-tui-mockup}` exactly once per landing page as the hero centerpiece. Never use the dark surface for body content.
- Reserve `{colors.accent}` (Apple Blue) and the rest of the semantic ramp for in-TUI states; marketing chrome stays monochrome.
- Use `{rounded.sm}` (4px) on every interactive element and `{rounded.none}` (0px) on every container.
- Stack content sections at `{spacing.section}` (96px) rhythm with only 1px `{colors.hairline}` rules between them.

### Don't
- Don't introduce a sans-serif body font, a display face, or an italic style. Berkeley Mono carries everything.
- Don't add drop shadows, gradients, or atmospheric backgrounds. The system is flat-on-cream.
- Don't replace the ASCII bracket markers with SVG icons. The brackets are the icons.
- Don't use the semantic accent ramp (`{colors.accent}`, `{colors.warning}`, `{colors.danger}`, `{colors.success}`) on marketing CTAs. They belong to the in-product TUI.
- Don't pad cards with 24px+ internal padding. List rows sit at 8px vertical; FAQ rows at 12px.
- Don't render the OpenCode wordmark as a vector logo. It is always block-pixel ASCII.
- Don't fill the hero TUI mockup with photography or illustration. It is text-only and always shows a faux terminal command line.

## Responsive Behavior

### Breakpoints

| Name | Width | Key Changes |
|---|---|---|
| desktop-large | 1280px+ | Default — 960px content column, 5-up footer link grid |
| desktop | 1024px | Same layout; nav remains horizontal |
| tablet | 850px | Footer collapses to 2-up grid; `/enterprise` two-column form stacks |
| tablet-narrow | 768px | Primary nav becomes hamburger drawer; Download CTA stays visible |
| mobile | 640px | Single-column everything; hero display drops 38px → ~28px; section padding tightens |

### Touch Targets
All interactive elements meet WCAG AA at the ~36–40px height range. `{component.button-primary}` sits at ~36px with 20px horizontal padding. `{component.text-input}` and `{component.textarea}` sit at ~40px. `{component.button-tab}` rows in the install-method strip sit at ~32–36px depending on label length but extend to a full 44px tappable cell via inline padding. Footer links use `{typography.caption-md}` (14px) but receive ~28px line-height (caption-md is 2.0) plus 8px vertical padding for a comfortable ~44px tappable row.

### Collapsing Strategy
- **Primary nav:** desktop horizontal cluster → tablet-narrow hamburger drawer at 768px. The dark "Download" CTA stays visible at all widths.
- **Hero TUI mockup:** maintains its full-bleed dark surface at every breakpoint; the ASCII wordmark scales proportionally and the keybinding-hint row may wrap to two lines on narrow screens.
- **Install snippet + tab strip:** desktop fixed-width pill → mobile full-width pill with horizontal scroll on the tab strip if labels overflow.
- **Footer:** 5-up horizontal link grid → 2-up at tablet → 1-up at mobile (each link becomes a full-width row).
- **`/enterprise` two-column layout:** desktop 50/50 → tablet stacks to single-column with the form below the text block.
- **Section padding:** `{spacing.section}` (96px) desktop → 64px tablet → 48px mobile.
- **Hero headline:** `{typography.display-xl}` (38px) at desktop, scaling to ~28px at mobile, line-height holding at 1.5.

### Image Behavior
There are no raster images in the system aside from the favicon and OG share image. Every visual element — wordmarks, charts, icons — is rendered as type or inline SVG and scales without aspect-ratio considerations.

## Iteration Guide

1. Focus on ONE component at a time. Pull its YAML entry and verify every property resolves.
2. Reference component names and tokens directly (`{colors.ink}`, `{component.hero-tui-mockup}`, `{rounded.sm}`) — do not paraphrase.
3. Run `npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md` after edits — `broken-ref`, `contrast-ratio`, and `orphaned-tokens` warnings flag issues automatically.
4. Add new variants as separate component entries (`-active`, `-disabled`) — do not bury them inside prose.
5. Default body to `{typography.body-md}`; reach for `{typography.body-strong}` for emphasis; reserve `{typography.display-xl}` strictly for the page-top hero headline.
6. Keep `{colors.surface-dark}` scarce — at most one full-bleed dark mockup per page. The dark surface is a narrative device, not a chrome treatment.
7. When introducing a new component, ask whether it can be expressed with the existing ASCII-bracket + 4px-radius + Berkeley-Mono vocabulary before adding new tokens. The system's strength is that it almost never needs new ones.

## Known Gaps

- **Mobile screenshots not captured** — responsive behavior synthesizes OpenCode's mobile pattern (hamburger drawer, single-column, footer accordion) from desktop evidence and the breakpoint stack.
- **Hover states not documented** by system policy.
- **In-product TUI screenshots** beyond the marketing hero mockup are not in the captured set; the actual `opencode` terminal interface (full keybindings, panels, status bar) is not documented here.
- **`/go` page** not extracted — the marketing page for the Go SDK likely shares the same chrome but introduces code-sample blocks not documented above.
- **Form validation state styling** (success / error inline messages) not present in the captured surfaces.

## Overview

Oracle's web system is unusual for an enterprise brand in that it barely uses colour at all. The page ground is a six-step ladder of warm neutrals that runs from pure white through three off-whites to a warm near-black, and that ladder does almost all the structural work. Sections are distinguished from one another not by cards or rules or shadows but by which rung of the ladder they sit on, stacked full-bleed and square-cornered so the page reads as a series of tonal shifts rather than a stack of containers.

The famous Oracle red appears exactly once per page, in the masthead wordmark, and nowhere else. Every action on the site is carried by `{colors.primary}`, a warm dark charcoal, in a small 4px-radius button that never grows louder than its label. The restraint is deliberate and total: there is no coloured CTA, no accent-tinted card, no gradient. When colour does arrive it arrives at full-band scale, a whole section width of `{colors.band-teal}` or `{colors.band-forest}`, and then the page returns to neutral.

What gives the system its character is the type. Two display registers run side by side. The corporate index sets its headings in Oracle Sans at weight 300, very large and very light, while the product pages set theirs in Georgia, a bookish transitional serif that is genuinely surprising on a database landing page. Beneath both, Oracle Sans handles everything else across a wide weight range, dropping to 350 for running copy and jumping all the way to 800 for section headings, so the contrast between a paragraph and the heading above it is enormous without either changing size very much. A single gold rule, 40 by 4 pixels, sits under the hero headline. It is the only decorative mark in the system, and against this much neutral it does a lot of work.

**Key Characteristics:**
- A six-rung warm neutral ladder — `{colors.canvas}` → `{colors.canvas-soft}` → `{colors.canvas-tint}` → `{colors.canvas-warm}` → `{colors.hairline}` → `{colors.ink-deep}` — carrying nearly every surface
- `{colors.brand-mark}` reserved for the wordmark and used nowhere else in the interface
- Every action in one warm charcoal `{colors.primary}` at `{rounded.xs}`, with no coloured CTA anywhere
- Two display registers, being Oracle Sans at weight 300 on the corporate index and Georgia serif across the product pages
- An extreme body-to-heading weight jump, from 350/400 running copy straight to 800 section headings
- Full-bleed square-cornered bands with no shadows — depth comes from tonal steps alone
- A 40 × 4px `{colors.accent-gold}` rule under the hero headline as the system's only ornament
- Chromatic colour deployed only at whole-band scale, never on a control

## Colors

### Brand & Accent
- **Oracle Red** (`{colors.brand-mark}` — #c74634): the wordmark, and only the wordmark. It appears in the masthead at the top of every page and is not used for any button, link, border, band or highlight. Elsewhere on the page red shows up only inside photography and inside logos printed on product hardware.
- **Action Charcoal** (`{colors.primary}` — #312d2a): the fill behind every primary action on the site. Warm rather than neutral, and a clear step lighter than `{colors.ink}` so a filled button reads as an object rather than as a block of text.
- **Action Charcoal Pressed** (`{colors.primary-pressed}` — #47423e): the active state of that button.
- **On Primary** (`{colors.on-primary}` — #ffffff): the label on a filled action, and the text colour on every inverted surface.
- **Gold Rule** (`{colors.accent-gold}` — #f0cc71): a 40 × 4px bar sitting under the hero headline on every product page. The system's one piece of ornament.
- **Gold Tab** (`{colors.accent-gold-soft}` — #f7e0a1): a paler gold, 5px tall, marking the selected item in the dark product sub-navigation.

### Surface
The surface set is a numbered ladder, and its rungs are close enough together that a band change reads as a shift in light rather than as a new panel.

- **Canvas** (`{colors.canvas}` — #ffffff): the masthead, the footer, content cards, and the brightest section bands.
- **Canvas Soft** (`{colors.canvas-soft}` — #fbf9f8): the most common product-page section fill. One barely-perceptible step off white.
- **Canvas Tint** (`{colors.canvas-tint}` — #f5f4f2): the next step, used for supporting sections and the contact hero.
- **Canvas Warm** (`{colors.canvas-warm}` — #f1efed): the warmest and most-used tint, carrying the corporate index page almost end to end and every product hero band.
- **Hairline** (`{colors.hairline}` — #e4e1dd): the tile and disabled-control border, and the last neutral rung before the dark end.
- **Divider** (`{colors.divider}` — #e9e7e4): the 2px vertical rule that separates the contact page's channel columns.
- **Field Border** (`{colors.field-border}` — #d4cfca): the 1px border around the masthead search field, one clear step darker than `{colors.hairline}` so an input reads as interactive against a card that merely reads as a container.
- **Ink Deep** (`{colors.ink-deep}` — #211e1c): the dark end of the ladder, used as a full-width band behind the product sub-navigation.

### Text
- **Ink** (`{colors.ink}` — #161513): every heading and every line of body copy. A warm near-black, never pure black, which keeps the very light 300-weight display sizes from looking harsh.
- **Link** (`{colors.link}` — #006b8f): inline links in body copy and channel columns. A deep teal-blue, set without an underline, at the same size and weight as the text around it — the colour alone carries the affordance.
- On dark bands, text inverts to `{colors.on-primary}` and there is no intermediate tone; the system has one text colour per polarity.

### Semantic
- **Focus** (`{colors.focus}` — #227e9e): the focus indicator, declared once and applied identically on light and dark surfaces, so a keyboard user sees the same ring everywhere.
- **Error** (`{colors.error}` — #d63b25): validation messaging and error field text.
- **Disabled Ink** (`{colors.disabled-ink}` — #aea8a2): the label on a disabled control, paired with a `{colors.canvas-soft}` fill and a `{colors.hairline}` border.

### Band Colours
Chromatic colour enters the system only as a full section band, never as a control, a card or a border.
- **Band Teal** (`{colors.band-teal}` — #d6e5e5): a pale teal strip, roughly 120 to 160px tall, used to break a run of neutral sections.
- **Band Forest** (`{colors.band-forest}` — #33553c): a deep green band carrying white text and a multi-column link list, around 390px tall.

## Typography

### Font Family
Three families, with a clear division of labour.

**Oracle Sans** is the workhorse — a variable humanist sans with open apertures and a slightly squared construction. Its variable axis is exercised hard: the declared base weight is 350, running copy sits at 350 or 400, and section headings jump all the way to 800. It also supplies the corporate index's display sizes at weight 300.

**Georgia** is the display serif on the product pages. It carries h1, h2 and h3 at 36 to 56px in regular weight, with its bracketed serifs and ball terminals reading as distinctly bookish next to the sans beneath it. It is declared as an explicit stack led by Georgia, so it renders as Georgia on virtually every machine rather than falling back.

**Consolas** is declared for monospace and never appears in page chrome.

### Hierarchy

| Token | Size | Weight | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{typography.display-serif-xl}` | 56px | 400 | 67.2px | 0 | Product hero headline, Georgia |
| `{typography.display-serif-lg}` | 40px | 400 | 48px | 0 | Major section headline, Georgia |
| `{typography.display-serif-md}` | 36px | 400 | 43.2px | 0 | Product page headline and section headline, Georgia |
| `{typography.display-sans-lg}` | 40px | 300 | 52px | 0 | Corporate index section headline, Oracle Sans Light |
| `{typography.display-sans-md}` | 32px | 300 | 44px | 0 | Corporate index page headline, Oracle Sans Light |
| `{typography.heading-xl}` | 28px | 800 | 33.6px | 0 | Product section heading |
| `{typography.heading-lg}` | 24px | 800 | 28.8px | 0 | Section and channel-column heading |
| `{typography.heading-md}` | 20px | 800 | 24px | 0 | Sub-section heading |
| `{typography.heading-sm}` | 18px | 800 | 21.6px | 0 | Card heading |
| `{typography.heading-card}` | 24px | 600 | 32px | 0 | Corporate index card heading |
| `{typography.lead}` | 24px | 400 | 33.6px | 0 | Standfirst paragraph under a hero |
| `{typography.body}` | 16px | 400 | 22.4px | 0 | Product page running copy and links |
| `{typography.body-loose}` | 16px | 350 | 24px | 0 | Corporate index running copy, at the declared base weight |
| `{typography.body-strong}` | 16px | 700 | 22.4px | 0 | Emphasised list item and inline lead-in |
| `{typography.label}` | 14px | 500 | 16.8px | 0 | Button label |
| `{typography.label-strong}` | 14px | 600 | 20px | 0 | Navigation tile label |
| `{typography.caption}` | 12px | 400 | 20px | 0 | Footer links and fine print |

### Principles
Letter-spacing is zero on every role without exception. There is no tracked-out eyebrow, no tightened display line, no small-caps label — the system leaves the typeface's own fitting alone at every size from 12px to 56px.

Line-height moves in two registers. Display and heading roles run at a tight 1.2 (67.2/56, 48/40, 28.8/24, 21.6/18 all resolve to exactly 1.2), while body roles open up to 1.4 (22.4/16) or 1.5 (24/16). The split is clean: anything that is a heading is set tight, anything that is read in sentences is set loose.

The weight range is the most distinctive thing about the system. Running copy sits at 350 or 400 and section headings sit at 800, with almost nothing in between, so hierarchy is carried by weight far more than by size. A 24px 800-weight heading over 16px 400-weight body is a much sharper break than the 1.5× size ratio alone would suggest. The 300-weight display sizes on the corporate index run in the opposite direction, being lighter than the body text they sit above.

### Note on Font Substitutes
**Oracle Sans** is a proprietary variable face. The closest open substitute is **Inter**, which shares the humanist skeleton and open apertures and offers a full variable weight axis including the 350 and 800 stops this system depends on; **Source Sans 3** is a warmer alternative but tops out lower and needs the 800 roles dropped to 700. **Georgia** ships with virtually every operating system and needs no substitution; if a webfont is required, **Gelasio** is metric-compatible with it. **Consolas** substitutes cleanly with **JetBrains Mono**. Keep the 1.2 heading line-height, the 1.4 body line-height, and zero tracking on any substitute.

## Layout

### Spacing System
- **Base unit**: 8px, though the working steps are finer at the small end and jump hard at the large end.
- **Tokens**: `{spacing.xs}` 10px · `{spacing.sm}` 12px · `{spacing.md}` 16px · `{spacing.lg}` 18px · `{spacing.xl}` 20px · `{spacing.xxl}` 24px · `{spacing.xxxl}` 32px · `{spacing.section}` 48px · `{spacing.gutter}` 72px
- `{spacing.section}` is the universal rhythm constant. Every full-width section on every page is padded `48px 0`, which is what gives the band stack its regularity.
- `{spacing.xxxl}` is the grid gutter and the corporate index card interior; `{spacing.xxl}` is the product card interior.
- Button padding is a fixed `10px 16px` everywhere, and headings carry an 18px bottom margin.

### Grid & Container
- **Outer container**: 1744px maximum, with a 72px side gutter.
- **Context container**: 1600px maximum for content that sits inside a band.
- **Minimum container**: 272px, which is the floor the layout collapses toward on the narrowest phones.
- **Grid gap**: 32px between columns, used by the corporate index tile row, the channel columns and the product card grids.
- **Masthead**: 85px tall, full width, white. **Product sub-navigation**: 64px, full width, sticky. **Footer**: 105px, full width, white.
- Sections are full-bleed and square-cornered; the container only constrains the content inside them, never the band itself.

### Whitespace Philosophy
Space is used to make the tonal ladder legible. Because adjacent bands can differ by as little as four or five points of lightness, each one needs enough vertical room for the eye to register it as a separate region — hence the uniform 48px section padding and the willingness to give a 160px teal strip an entire band to itself. Inside a band the opposite applies: content is packed into a 1600px column with 32px gutters and relatively tight card padding, so the generous outer rhythm reads as structure rather than emptiness.

### Responsive Strategy

#### Breakpoints
| Name | Width | Key Changes |
|---|---|---|
| Small mobile | ≤ 450px | Single column throughout; masthead collapses to hamburger, wordmark and icons; tile row stacks |
| Mobile | 451–600px | The system's heaviest breakpoint — sub-navigation becomes a scrolling strip, card grids go 1-up, hero type drops to its floor |
| Tablet | 601–770px | The second heaviest — grids go 2-up, the search field collapses to an icon, channel columns stack and lose their dividers |
| Laptop | 771–974px | 2-up and 3-up grids, side gutters tighten from 72px toward the container minimum |
| Desktop | 975–1344px | Full multi-column grids, sub-navigation shows all items inline |
| Wide | 1345–1744px | Content reaches the 1600px context cap; bands continue full-bleed |
| Ultra-wide | ≥ 1744px | Outer container caps; surplus width is absorbed by the band fills on either side |

#### Touch Targets
`{components.button-primary}` stands 37px tall at its 10px vertical padding and 14px label, which is under the 44×44 WCAG AAA minimum and relies on surrounding margin for comfortable tapping. `{components.text-input}` and `{components.product-subnav}` both clear it comfortably, at roughly 46px and 64px respectively, as does `{components.nav-tile}`. For rebuilds, raising the button's vertical padding to 14px brings it to 45px without changing any other value in the system.

#### Collapsing Strategy
The masthead is the element that changes most: at desktop it carries a hamburger, the wordmark, a wide search field and three utility icons, and below tablet the search field collapses to an icon while the rest holds position. The product sub-navigation keeps its full-bleed band at every width and turns into a horizontally scrolling strip rather than wrapping, so the active `{components.subnav-active-bar}` stays visible. Card grids step 4-up to 3-up to 2-up to 1-up across the ladder. The channel columns on the contact page drop their `{colors.divider}` vertical rules when they stack, since a vertical rule between stacked blocks reads as a mistake. Section padding holds at `{spacing.section}` far longer than most systems would keep it, compressing only at the mobile breakpoints.

#### Image Behavior
Photography is full-bleed inside its container and square-cornered when it fills a band, but takes `{rounded.md}` when it sits inside a product card and `{rounded.xl}` when it fills half of a corporate index content card. Video thumbnails carry a circular `{components.play-button-circular}` overlay. The contact hero uses a cut-out photographic strip with a soft feathered lower edge rather than a hard crop. Decorative pattern overlays — fine topographic contour lines, large open swirls — sit behind hero content at very low contrast and are treated as part of the band fill rather than as images.

## Elevation & Depth

| Level | Treatment | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Flat fill on the neutral ladder | Every band, section, nav and footer — the default |
| 1 | One rung up or down the ladder | Cards on a tinted band, the dark sub-navigation strip |
| 2 | 1px `{colors.hairline}` border | Navigation tiles and disabled controls |

The system carries **no shadows at all**. Not on cards, not on the sticky sub-navigation, not on the masthead, not on modals. Depth is produced entirely by position on the neutral ladder: a white card on a `{colors.canvas-warm}` band reads as raised because it is lighter, and a `{colors.ink-deep}` sub-navigation reads as a distinct plane because it is far darker. Where two surfaces sit on the same rung, a 1px `{colors.hairline}` border does the separating instead.

There are no gradients in the page chrome. The only tonal transitions in the system are the feathered lower edge of a cut-out hero photograph and the angled diagonal that ends some hero bands, and both belong to the image, not to the surface.

### Decorative Depth
Hero bands carry very low-contrast pattern overlays — dense topographic contour lines on one product page, large open swirls on another — drawn a point or two off the band fill. They read as texture rather than as image, and they are the reason a large area of `{colors.canvas-warm}` does not feel empty. Some hero bands end on an angled diagonal rather than a horizontal edge, letting the following band cut up into them.

## Shapes

### Border Radius Scale

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{rounded.none}` | 0px | Every band, section, masthead, sub-navigation and footer |
| `{rounded.xs}` | 4px | Every button, and every anchor styled as a button |
| `{rounded.sm}` | 6px | The masthead search field and small column items |
| `{rounded.md}` | 8px | Product page cards and media frames |
| `{rounded.lg}` | 12px | Corporate index navigation tiles |
| `{rounded.xl}` | 15px | Corporate index content cards and their inner stat panels |
| `{rounded.full}` | 9999px | The circular video play control |

The scale is unusually fine-grained at the small end, with 4, 6 and 8 all in active use and each assigned to a different control family — buttons, fields, cards. The two large steps are template-specific rather than interchangeable: the corporate index uses 15px throughout while the product pages use 8px, so a card's radius tells you which template you are on. The 15px value is worth noting as a deliberate oddity, since 16px would be the conventional choice and the system consistently uses 15.

### Photography Geometry
Images inside product cards take `{rounded.md}`; images filling half a corporate index card take `{rounded.xl}`. Full-band photography is square-cornered. Aspect ratios are not fixed — video thumbnails run roughly 16:9, hero photography is a wide strip, and card imagery fills whatever the card gives it. The system never crops to a circle except for the play control.

**`hero-eyebrow-rule`**
- Background `{colors.accent-gold}`, rounded `{rounded.none}`, 40 × 4px
- Sits directly under the hero headline. The system's only ornament

**`section-band-white`** · **`section-band-soft`** · **`section-band-tint`** · **`section-band-warm`**
- Backgrounds `{colors.canvas}`, `{colors.canvas-soft}`, `{colors.canvas-tint}` and `{colors.canvas-warm}` respectively
- All text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body}`, rounded `{rounded.none}`, padding `48px`
- The four neutral rungs. A page is built by alternating them; the shift between adjacent rungs is deliberately small

**`section-band-teal`**
- Background `{colors.band-teal}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body}`, rounded `{rounded.none}`, padding `48px`
- A short chromatic strip, around 120 to 160px tall, used to interrupt a long neutral run

**`section-band-forest`**
- Background `{colors.band-forest}`, text `{colors.on-primary}`, type `{typography.body}`, rounded `{rounded.none}`, padding `48px`
- The one deep colour band, carrying white text and a multi-column link list

### Cards & Media

**`content-card`**
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body-loose}`, rounded `{rounded.xl}`, padding `{spacing.xxxl}`
- The corporate index workhorse. A wide card holding a headline, copy, a primary action and a half-width image

**`stat-panel`**
- Background `{colors.canvas-warm}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body-loose}`, rounded `{rounded.xl}`, padding `{spacing.xl}`
- A tinted block nested inside a content card, holding a short bulleted list of figures

**`product-card`** and **`product-card-warm`**
- Backgrounds `{colors.canvas}` and `{colors.canvas-warm}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.xxl}`
- The product page equivalent, at the smaller radius. The warm variant is used when the card sits on a white band

**`nav-tile`**
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.label-strong}`, 1px `{colors.hairline}` border, rounded `{rounded.lg}`, padding `{spacing.md}`
- The row of eight product entry tiles below the corporate index masthead, grouped under two light sans labels

**`media-frame`**
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`
- The frame around an embedded video or product screenshot

**`play-button-circular`**
- Background `{colors.ink}`, icon `{colors.on-primary}`, rounded `{rounded.full}`, 40px
- The only circular element in the system

### Content & Links

**`channel-column`**
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.heading-lg}`, 2px `{colors.divider}` rule, rounded `{rounded.none}`, padding `{spacing.xxl}`
- A three-up group on the contact page. Each column holds a thin outline icon, an 800-weight heading, a short paragraph and a `{components.link-inline}`, separated by full-height vertical rules

**`link-inline`**
- Text `{colors.link}`, type `{typography.body}`, rounded `{rounded.none}`
- Set with no underline and at the same size and weight as the surrounding copy

### Footer

**`footer`**
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.caption}`, rounded `{rounded.none}`, 105px tall
- A single horizontal row of fine-print links above a row of social icons. No rule, no fill change, no column structure

**`footer-link`**
- Text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.caption}`, rounded `{rounded.none}`
- Set in ink rather than `{colors.link}`, which is what keeps the footer quiet

### Examples (illustrative)

> These ten surfaces are kit-mirror demonstrations, not components found on the brand's own pages. Each is composed from the primitives above so downstream consumers re-skin the shapes this system actually uses — the square `{rounded.none}` band, the `{rounded.xs}` button, the `{rounded.md}` card, and a neutral ladder that separates surfaces by tone and a hairline rule instead of by shadow.

**`ex-pricing-tier`** — default tier card
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, 1px `{colors.hairline}` border, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.xxl}`
- CTA from `{components.button-secondary}`

**`ex-pricing-tier-featured`** — the highlighted tier
- Background `{colors.primary}`, text `{colors.on-primary}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.xxl}`
- Polarity-flipped to the action charcoal, the same inversion `{components.section-band-forest}` performs, with its CTA from `{components.button-primary-inverse}`

**`ex-product-selector`** — what's-included summary card
- Background `{colors.canvas-soft}`, text `{colors.ink}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.xxl}`
- One rung up the ladder, with rows borrowing `{components.nav-tile}` chrome

**`ex-cart-drawer`** — subscription summary
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.xxl}`, line items separated by `{colors.divider}`
- The same warm rule `{components.channel-column}` uses between columns

**`ex-app-shell-row`** — sidebar nav row
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.sm} {spacing.md}`, active indicator `{colors.primary}`

**`ex-data-table-cell`** — table header and body chrome
- Header background `{colors.canvas-tint}` in `{typography.caption}`, body cells `{typography.body}`, cell padding `{spacing.sm} {spacing.md}`, row border `{colors.hairline}`

**`ex-auth-form-card`** — sign-in card
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, 1px `{colors.hairline}` border, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.xxl}`
- Inputs take the `{components.text-input}` treatment

**`ex-modal-card`** — modal dialog surface
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, 1px `{colors.hairline}` border, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.xxl}`
- No shadow, since the system has none — the modal is bounded by its rule alone

**`ex-empty-state-card`** — empty-state frame
- Background `{colors.canvas-soft}`, text `{colors.ink}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.section}`, caption in `{typography.body}`

**`ex-toast`** — toast notification surface
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body}`, 1px `{colors.hairline}` border, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding `{spacing.sm} {spacing.xl}`

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Build page structure from the neutral ladder. Moving a section one rung is the system's way of saying "new region".
- Keep `{colors.brand-mark}` on the wordmark and nowhere else. Its scarcity is what gives it weight.
- Run every action through `{colors.primary}` at `{rounded.xs}` with `10px 16px` padding, whatever the context.
- Flip polarity rather than changing colour when an action lands on a dark band — use `{components.button-primary-inverse}`.
- Hold `{spacing.section}` at 48px on every full-width band; the uniform rhythm is what makes the small tonal steps legible.
- Let weight carry hierarchy. The 400-to-800 jump between body and heading is the system's main structural signal.
- Keep letter-spacing at zero on every role, at every size.
- Deploy chromatic colour only at whole-band scale, as `{components.section-band-teal}` or `{components.section-band-forest}`.

### Don't
- Don't add shadows. The system has none, and elevation is expressed by position on the neutral ladder.
- Don't use pure black. `{colors.ink}` is warm and deliberately a few points off it.
- Don't round a band, a section, a masthead or a footer — `{rounded.none}` on full-width chrome is the rule.
- Don't mix the two card radii. `{rounded.xl}` belongs to the corporate index and `{rounded.md}` to the product pages; using both on one page breaks the template read.
- Don't set a headline in Oracle Sans on a product page or in Georgia on the corporate index — the two registers do not cross templates.
- Don't underline `{components.link-inline}`; `{colors.link}` alone carries the affordance.
- Don't add a fourth or fifth tint between the ladder rungs. They are already close enough that another step would be invisible.
- Don't give `{components.hero-eyebrow-rule}` a second colour or a second instance per page; one 40 × 4px gold bar is the whole ornament budget.

---


## Overview

Oura's web presence reads like a printed field journal that learned to breathe. The default surface is a warm paper cream (`{colors.canvas}` — #f7f1e8) rather than white, and everything sits on it with generous air: a light, high-contrast serif for the big statements, a calm grotesque sans for everything you actually read, and full-bleed lifestyle photography that carries most of the emotional weight. Where a typical wellness-tech site would reach for gradients and glassmorphism, Oura reaches for restraint — flat fills, hairline rules, and long vertical silences between sections.

The system runs three surface "worlds." The **cream world** (`{colors.canvas}`) is home base for marketing and editorial content. The **ink world** (`{colors.ink-band}` / `{colors.ink-band-soft}`) is a near-black stage reserved for the footer and the "In the News" band, where cream cards float like clippings on a dark table. The **silver world** (`{colors.surface-grey}` → `{colors.silver}`) is a cool, machined grey gradient used only on the product-showcase pages, where the ring is photographed like jewellery.

Color discipline is the signature move. The whole palette is earth-toned — mustard and gold (`{colors.gold}`, `{colors.ochre}`), clay and espresso (`{colors.clay}`, `{colors.espresso}`), olive and sage (`{colors.forest}`, `{colors.sage}`) — and these appear as accent bands, illustration, and score/data-visualisation, never as buttons. Buttons carry a single, deliberate exception: **action blue** (`{colors.primary}` — #2a72de), used only for the decisive conversion moments ("Explore", "Shop All Products"). The warm brand neutral `{colors.stone}` (#4a4741) does the quieter work — the wordmark, editorial pills, form fields, outlines, and links — so the blue never has to compete.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Warm-paper canvas (`{colors.canvas}`) as the default surface, not white — cream is the brand's resting state.
- A two-typeface voice: `{typography.display}` (Editorial New, a light high-contrast serif) for headlines, `{typography.body}` (AkkuratLL, a neutral grotesque) for reading.
- One decisive **action blue** (`{colors.primary}`) reserved strictly for primary CTAs; every other button is warm-neutral `{colors.stone}` or cream.
- An earth-tone accent family — mustard, clay, olive — used for bands, illustration and data-viz, deliberately kept off buttons.
- Fully-rounded pill buttons (`{rounded.full}`) against softly-rounded cards (`{rounded.lg}`) and large-radius product images (`{rounded.xl}`).
- Three surface worlds cycling in a predictable rhythm: cream editorial → black news/footer band → silver product stage.
- Photography-first hierarchy: full-bleed imagery leads, UI recedes to hairlines and quiet labels.

## Colors

> Source pages analysed: the homepage, the Oura Ring 5 store page, the Activity & Movement page, and the Clinical & Science Experts page. The palette below reconciles all four into one system.

### Brand & Accent
- **Action Blue** (`{colors.primary}` — #2a72de): the single conversion color. Fills the primary CTA pill ("Explore", "Shop All Products") with `{colors.on-primary}` text. Used nowhere else — not for links, not for accents.
- **Stone** (`{colors.stone}` — #4a4741): the warm taupe-brown brand neutral. Carries the wordmark, secondary/editorial pill buttons, form-field fills, circular-icon outlines, and default link color. This is the color that makes Oura feel "Oura."
- **Clay** (`{colors.clay}` — #6b443d): a warm reddish-brown used for accent bands and content cards (e.g., the Activity page's "Your Oura Activity Score" band).
- **Espresso** (`{colors.espresso}` — #39221e): the darkest brown, for deep accent fills and rich text on gold surfaces.
- **Gold** (`{colors.gold}` — #af751b) / **Ochre** (`{colors.ochre}` — #bc924c) / **Gold Soft** (`{colors.gold-soft}` — #ddaa61) / **Gold Pale** (`{colors.gold-pale}` — #ddbe78) / **Gold Deep** (`{colors.gold-deep}` — #684d07): the mustard ramp. Powers warm illustration, the activity-ring dashboard card, and score data-visualisation.
- **Forest** (`{colors.forest}` — #224228) / **Olive** (`{colors.olive}` — #5c6f5d) / **Sage** (`{colors.sage}` — #849671) / **Sage Mute** (`{colors.sage-mute}` — #7b886d) / **Sage Pale** (`{colors.sage-pale}` — #ced4b8): the olive ramp, used for calm accent bands, illustration, and secondary data-visualisation.

### Surface
- **Canvas** (`{colors.canvas}` — #f7f1e8): the signature warm-paper background for all editorial and marketing surfaces.
- **Surface** (`{colors.surface}` — #ffffff): pure white, for elevated cards, inputs-on-cream, and the circular "+" overlay buttons on person cards.
- **Surface Grey** (`{colors.surface-grey}` — #ececec): the light end of the product-page gradient and light utility fills.
- **Silver** (`{colors.silver}` — #cccac7): the cool grey used on product-showcase pages and as the selected-tab border.
- **Ink Band** (`{colors.ink-band}` — #000000): the true-black stage for the footer / news band.
- **Ink Band Soft** (`{colors.ink-band-soft}` — #19191c): the near-black used for the footer surface, a hair warmer than pure black.
- **Hairline** (`{colors.hairline}` — #e1dcd3): the warm 1px divider on cream (a low-opacity ink wash blended onto canvas).

### Text
- **Ink** (`{colors.ink}` — #1c1b1a): primary heading and body text on cream.
- **Stone** (`{colors.stone}` — #4a4741): secondary text and editorial emphasis on cream.
- **Ash** (`{colors.ash}` — #838280): muted grey for meta text, titles-under-names, and utility captions.
- **Mute** (`{colors.mute}` — #a8a5a0): warm grey for the quietest captions and for secondary text on dark bands.
- **On Dark** (`{colors.on-dark}` — #ffffff): text and icons on the ink and silver worlds.

### Semantic
- **Error** (`{colors.error}` — #e33a22): validation and focus-error state on form fields (the focused email field border).

## Typography

### Font Family
Two families carry the entire system, and the tension between them is the point.

- **Editorial New** (`{typography.display}`, `{typography.heading-1}`, `{typography.heading-2}`, `{typography.lead}`): a light, high-contrast transitional serif used for display headlines, section titles, and the occasional light-serif lead paragraph. Weights run thin — 100 and 300 — so the large sizes read as elegant, not heavy. The Activity page shows it in italic ("move *count*") for a hand-set editorial flourish.
- **AkkuratLL** (`{typography.heading-3}` through `{typography.caption}`): a neutral Swiss grotesque that does all the real reading work — subheads, body, UI labels, buttons, captions. Weights 300 / 400 / 600 / 700.

### Hierarchy

| Token | Family | Size | Weight | Line Height | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{typography.display}` | Editorial New | 110px | 300 | 1.05 | Homepage hero headline ("Subtle. Power.") |
| `{typography.display-2}` | Editorial New | 80px | 300 | 1.1 | Secondary-page display headlines |
| `{typography.heading-1}` | Editorial New | 68px | 300 | 1.1 | Large page titles |
| `{typography.heading-2}` | Editorial New | 40px | 300 | 1.15 | Section headlines |
| `{typography.heading-3}` | AkkuratLL | 40px | 400 | 1.25 | Sans section headings / large stats |
| `{typography.title}` | AkkuratLL | 32px | 400 | 1.25 | Card titles, sub-section titles |
| `{typography.lead}` | Editorial New | 24px | 100 | 1.25 | Light-serif intro / lead paragraphs |
| `{typography.body-lg}` | AkkuratLL | 20px | 400 | 1.5 | Emphasised body copy |
| `{typography.body}` | AkkuratLL | 18px | 400 | 1.5 | Default body text |
| `{typography.body-sm}` | AkkuratLL | 16px | 400 | 1.5 | Dense body, links, form text |
| `{typography.button}` | AkkuratLL | 16px | 600 | 1 | Button labels |
| `{typography.ui}` | AkkuratLL | 14px | 400 | 1.4 | Nav links, tabs, utility UI |
| `{typography.caption}` | AkkuratLL | 13px | 400 | 1.4 | Captions, footnotes |
| `{typography.eyebrow}` | AkkuratLL | 12px | 700 | 1.2 | Small-caps overlines ("IN THE NEWS", "FEATURED ARTICLE") |

### Principles
- Serif for feeling, sans for facts. `{typography.display}` and its siblings appear only at large sizes where the high stroke contrast is legible and expressive; everything at reading scale is `{typography.body}`.
- Thin display weights. Big serif headlines lean on weight 100–300, so scale — not boldness — creates hierarchy.
- Quiet overlines. Section context is set with `{typography.eyebrow}` (uppercase, lightly tracked) rather than heavy kickers.

### Note on Font Substitutes
Both faces are proprietary. For open-source builds, substitute **Editorial New** with **Fraunces** or **Newsreader** (both high-contrast serifs — set optical size high and weight low to match the thin display feel), and **AkkuratLL** with **Inter** or **Hanken Grotesk** (neutral grotesques with similar x-height). When substituting, nudge display line-height up slightly (Fraunces runs a touch taller than Editorial New) and keep body tracking at 0.

## Layout

### Spacing System
- **Base unit**: 8px.
- **Tokens**: `{spacing.xxs}` 4px · `{spacing.xs}` 8px · `{spacing.sm}` 12px · `{spacing.md}` 16px · `{spacing.lg}` 24px · `{spacing.xl}` 32px.
- Card interiors sit at `{spacing.lg}`; tight utility groupings (form padding, chip padding) at `{spacing.sm}`–`{spacing.md}`. Section-to-section rhythm is deliberately large — long vertical gaps of blank cream separate content blocks, letting photography and headlines breathe.

### Grid & Container
- Content is center-constrained within a wide max-width, with full-bleed photography breaking out to the viewport edges.
- Card grids run 3-up (person cards, benefit trios) and 4-up (news / expert carousels), collapsing toward 1-up on narrow screens.
- The product page alternates centered single-column showcases with edge-to-edge media.

### Whitespace Philosophy
Empty cream is a design element, not leftover space. Large silences between sections group related content and pace the scroll like chapters. UI chrome stays minimal so the eye rests on imagery and headlines.

### Responsive Strategy

#### Breakpoints
| Name | Width | Key Changes |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop | ≥ 1280px | Full multi-column grids, horizontal nav, large display type |
| Laptop | 1024–1279px | Slightly tightened gutters, same structure |
| Tablet | 768–1023px | 4-up grids → 2-up, nav begins to condense |
| Mobile | ≤ 767px | Single-column stacks, hamburger nav, display type scales down (110px → ~48px), pill CTAs go full-width-ish |

(Breakpoint ladder observed in the extracted media-query data spans 1280 → 1024 → 896 → 768 → 600 → 480 → 320px.)

#### Touch Targets
Pill buttons (`button-primary`, `button-secondary`) and circular icon buttons (`button-icon-circular`) are sized for comfortable tapping; keep interactive controls at a minimum 44×44px on touch. Carousel arrows and the "+" person-card buttons are circular and finger-sized.

#### Collapsing Strategy
- Horizontal nav collapses to a hamburger below the tablet breakpoint; the cart and wordmark persist.
- Multi-column card grids collapse 4-up → 2-up → 1-up.
- The silver product showcase keeps its centered single-column media on all sizes and simply scales the imagery.
- Footer link columns reflow from a 4-column row into stacked groups.

#### Image Behavior
Photography is full-bleed and art-directed, often edge-to-edge on mobile. Product imagery uses large-radius rounded frames (`{rounded.xl}`); editorial imagery is frequently un-rounded full-bleed. Images lazy-load as sections enter the viewport.

## Elevation & Depth

| Level | Treatment | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 0 — Flat | No shadow; separation by color-world shift or `{colors.hairline}` rule | Default on cream; most sections |
| 1 — Resting card | Very soft, low-opacity drop shadow | News cards on the black band, the Technical Specifications card |
| 2 — Floating | Slightly deeper, more diffuse soft shadow | Product-showcase media cards, elevated content cards |
| 3 — Overlay | Strong diffuse shadow + scrim | Modals / dialogs (rare) |

Depth is understated. On cream, sections separate through the surface-world shift (cream → black → silver) and hairline dividers rather than heavy elevation. Where shadows appear, they are soft, warm, and low-opacity — never hard or high-contrast.

### Decorative Depth
Depth mostly comes from **photography** (full-bleed lifestyle imagery, machined product renders on the silver stage) and from **warm accent bands** (`{colors.clay}`, `{colors.gold}` families) that recede or advance a section. Subtle radial glows appear behind product imagery on the store page to lift the ring off its grey backdrop.

## Shapes

### Border Radius Scale

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{rounded.none}` | 0px | Full-bleed imagery, bands, nav |
| `{rounded.xs}` | 4px | Small utility chips, tight controls |
| `{rounded.sm}` | 8px | Small cards, badges, list items |
| `{rounded.md}` | 12px | Form fields (email input) |
| `{rounded.lg}` | 24px | Content cards, person cards, news cards |
| `{rounded.xl}` | 40px | Large product-image cards on the store page |
| `{rounded.full}` | 9999px | Pill buttons, tabs, circular icon buttons, stat badges |

### Photography Geometry
Product and lifestyle imagery is generous and soft-cornered: product cards use `{rounded.xl}`, editorial and person imagery uses `{rounded.lg}` or runs full-bleed with no radius. Person cards are near-portrait rectangles with a small circular "+" affordance in the corner. Stat readouts ("99%", "95%", "90%") sit in perfect circles (`{rounded.full}`).

## Components

> Only Default and (where genuinely extracted) Active/Pressed states are documented. Variants live as separate `components:` entries in the front matter.

### Navigation

**`nav-bar`** — Top navigation on cream
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, links in `{colors.stone}` at `{typography.ui}`, no radius. Slots: OURA wordmark (left, `{colors.stone}`), center dropdown links (Shop, Your Health, Why Oura, For Organizations), cart icon (right). Sits flush on the cream canvas with no divider until scrolled.

**`announcement-bar`** — Top promo strip
- Full-width cream strip above the nav, centered `{typography.eyebrow}` text in `{colors.ink}` (e.g. free-trial offer copy). No radius, no background shift — it reads as the top edge of the paper.

### Hero

**`hero`** — Page-opening statement
- Cream background, `{typography.display}` serif headline in `{colors.ink}` (homepage: "Subtle. Power."), a small serif eyebrow label above, and a single `button-primary` blue pill CTA. Often paired with full-bleed product/lifestyle photography directly beneath the headline.

### Buttons

**`button-primary`** — Primary conversion CTA
- Background `{colors.primary}`, text `{colors.on-primary}`, type `{typography.button}`, fully rounded (`{rounded.full}`). The only blue in the interface. Used for "Explore" and "Shop All Products".

**`button-secondary`** — Editorial / secondary action
- Background `{colors.stone}`, text `{colors.on-stone}`, `{typography.button}`, `{rounded.full}`. The warm-neutral pill for content actions ("Why Oura", "How It Works").

**`button-on-dark`** — Cream pill on dark surfaces
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.stone}`, `{typography.button}`, `{rounded.full}`. Used for "Read More" and card actions floating on the black news band. (Extracted button variant: cream fill, stone text, full radius.)

**`button-outline`** — Outline pill on dark/photo
- Transparent over `{colors.ink-band}`, 1px `{colors.on-dark}` border, white text, `{rounded.full}`. For low-emphasis actions over dark imagery.

**`button-outline-stone`** — Outline pill on cream
- Cream background, 1px `{colors.stone}` border, `{colors.stone}` text, `{rounded.full}`. Low-emphasis action on the paper canvas.

**`button-icon-circular`** — Circular icon control
- Circular (`{rounded.full}`) control for carousel arrows and the person-card "+" affordance. Two flavours: a white surface circle (`{colors.surface}`) with a hairline edge for the "+" overlays, and a stone-outlined circle for the carousel arrows.

### Inputs & Forms

**`text-input`** — Newsletter / email field
- Background `{colors.stone}`, text `{colors.on-stone}`, `{typography.body-sm}`, radius `{rounded.md}` (12px), padding roughly 8px vertical / 20px left with a trailing submit affordance on the right. The dark taupe fill makes the field feel like part of the footer rather than a bright form box.

**`text-input-focused`** — Focused / error field
- On focus the field lifts to a light surface (`{colors.surface}`) with `{colors.ink}` text and a `{colors.error}` border for the validation-error state. Radius stays `{rounded.md}`.

### Cards & Containers

**`feature-card`** — Content / benefit card
- White surface (`{colors.surface}`), `{colors.hairline}` border, `{colors.ink}` text, `{typography.body}`, radius `{rounded.lg}`, padding `{spacing.lg}`. The default soft-cornered content container on cream.

**`feature-card-elevated`** — Floating content card
- Cream surface (`{colors.canvas}`) with a soft Level-1/2 shadow, `{rounded.lg}`, padding `{spacing.lg}`. Used where a card floats over imagery or the black band (news clippings, spec card).

**`product-card`** — Product-showcase media card
- Cool grey surface (`{colors.surface-grey}`), large radius `{rounded.xl}` (40px), holds a machined product render on the silver stage, often with a subtle radial glow behind the ring.

**`person-card`** — Expert / leadership card
- Cream background, portrait photo with radius `{rounded.lg}`, a white circular `button-icon-circular` "+" in the corner, name in `{typography.body}`/`{typography.title}` and role in `{colors.ash}` `{typography.caption}`. Appears in horizontal carousels.

**`news-card`** — News clipping on the dark band
- Cream card (`{colors.canvas}`) floating on `{colors.ink-band}`, `{colors.ink}` text, `{typography.body}`, `{rounded.lg}`, padding `{spacing.lg}`. Carries a publication quote plus a circular arrow link.

### Signature Components

**`stat-badge`** — Circular stat readout
- Perfect circle (`{rounded.full}`) on cream with a large `{typography.title}`/`{typography.heading-3}` number in `{colors.stone}` and a small caption beneath (e.g. "99% / 95% / 90%" accuracy figures on the product page).

**`pill-tab`** — Product selector tab
- Fully-rounded (`{rounded.full}`) tab in a horizontal selector row; selected state gets a `{colors.silver}` (2px) border, label in `{typography.ui}`, `{colors.stone}` text on cream. Used for the "Everyday health sensing" category switcher.

**`eyebrow-label`** — Section overline
- Uppercase `{typography.eyebrow}` label in `{colors.ink}` on cream, no background, marking section context ("ACTIVITY & MOVEMENT", "FROM THE PULSE BLOG", "FEATURED ARTICLE" as a small pill on imagery).

**`footer`** — Site footer
- Near-black surface (`{colors.ink-band-soft}`), `{colors.on-dark}` text and `{colors.mute}` secondary text, `{typography.body-sm}`. Contains the OURA wordmark, a newsletter `text-input`, payment-method icons, a 4-column link grid, and a language pill.

### Examples (illustrative)

> Auto-derived kit-mirror demonstration surfaces (`scripts/derive-examples-block.mjs`). Each `ex-*` entry references brand-native primitives so downstream consumers (`/preview-design`, `/generate-kit`) re-skin the same 10 surfaces consistently.

**`ex-pricing-tier`** — Default Pricing tier card. Re-uses feature-card chrome with brand canvas-soft surface.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `textColor`, `borderColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-pricing-tier-featured`** — Featured/highlighted tier — polarity-flipped surface (dark fill + light text in light mode, light fill + dark text in dark mode).
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `textColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-product-selector`** — Color/size picker chrome — fashion / DTC variant selector.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-cart-drawer`** — Shopping cart drawer — DTC / fashion brand actual cart chrome.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`, `item-divider`

**`ex-app-shell-row`** — Sidebar nav row inside the App Shell example. Active state uses brand primary as the indicator.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `activeIndicator`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-data-table-cell`** — Default data-table th + td chrome. Header uses mono-caps eyebrow typography; body uses body-sm.
- Properties: `headerBackground`, `headerTypography`, `bodyTypography`, `cellPadding`, `rowBorder`

**`ex-auth-form-card`** — Sign-in / sign-up card. Re-uses feature-card chrome with text-input primitives inside.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-modal-card`** — Modal dialog surface — same chrome as feature-card with elevated shadow.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-empty-state-card`** — Empty-state illustration frame.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`, `captionTypography`

**`ex-toast`** — Toast notification surface — feature-card shape + medium shadow.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`, `typography`


## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Reserve `{colors.primary}` strictly for the primary conversion CTA — one blue moment per view, maximum.
- Default every surface to `{colors.canvas}` (warm paper), not white. White (`{colors.surface}`) is for elevated cards and inputs, not backgrounds.
- Use `{colors.stone}` for the wordmark, secondary pills, outlines, form fills, and links — it is the workhorse neutral.
- Pair `{typography.display}` (thin serif) at large sizes with `{typography.body}` (grotesque) for reading; let scale create hierarchy.
- Keep pills fully rounded (`{rounded.full}`) and cards softly rounded (`{rounded.lg}`); use `{rounded.xl}` only for large product imagery.
- Let the earth-tone ramps (gold, clay, olive) live in bands, illustration, and data-viz — as color-blocked sections that pace the scroll.
- Give sections large vertical breathing room; treat empty cream as structure.

### Don't
- Don't use `{colors.primary}` for links, accents, icons, or decorative fills — it must stay unique to the primary CTA.
- Don't put the mustard/olive accent colors on buttons — they are surfaces and illustration, never actions.
- Don't set body copy in `{typography.display}`; the thin serif is display-only and gets illegible at small sizes.
- Don't default backgrounds to white — it breaks the warm-paper identity.
- Don't add heavy or hard-edged shadows; elevation here is soft, warm, and low-opacity.
- Don't crowd sections — compressing the vertical rhythm collapses the calm, editorial pacing that defines the brand.
